confidential: Prepared for Epik High • Client proposal
heroBody: Use the new music to build demand for the shows. Use the shows to bring fans back to the music.
heroRecBody: Six priority ticket flights. Two finishing bursts. Paid listening after every market. Includes $1,000 for creator outreach and negotiation management.
artCaption: Official EPIKASE SONG BATTLE artwork • Released 04 Sep 2026
opportunityIntro: A three-song release gives the tour three fresh ways in. The job is to turn that attention into a reason to choose a show, then give the night a life beyond the venue.
opportunityBody: Recommend the $15K campaign to deepen six ticket flights where the September 2 counts show the clearest need, add short Los Angeles and Oakland bursts, and double the paid listening flight after every market. The $10K campaign supports the same six priority cities with smaller allocations and paid listening after all 13 markets. Both totals include a $1,000 creator outreach and negotiation management line. The artist’s team supplies all finished creative; CCD manages strategy, paid media and creator coordination.
insight1: Atlanta has 1,264 open tickets at 44.6% sold. New York has 953 open with the tour’s earliest show, followed by Boston with 716. Prioritize those three alongside the added Seattle date, Las Vegas and Dallas. Use the listening geography to shape audiences and creative; the ticket report now sets the allocation.
insight2Title: Test the songs. Track the members.
insight2: The new tracks are credited to DJ TUKUTZ, TABLO and MITHRA JIN. Track each song directly, alongside Epik High’s group profile. Release-day streams and playlist data are unavailable in the API, so no song earns the lead by numbers yet.
insight3Title: Treat each show as its own decision.
insight3: The September 2 WME report shows 18,405 sold of 25,574 sellable tickets across 14 shows: 72.0% sold, with 7,169 open. Seattle October 25 is 45.5% sold; October 22 is 94.2% sold with 58 open. Direct Seattle ticket spend to October 25. Review fresh counts before each flight and pause sales ads when a show sells out.
baselineNote: Chartmetric API, retrieved Sep 4, 2026. Aug 31 non-interpolated endpoints; monthly listeners are rolling 28-day unique listeners, not streams. Followers are cumulative profile follows, not an addressable advertising list. These are pre-campaign observations, not campaign results.
releaseTitle:
Three personalities.
One Epik High night.
releaseIntro: Released September 4, 2026, EPIKASE SONG BATTLE brings three member-led tracks into one campaign for the North American tour.
track1Body: The official episode gives TUKUTZ a dance-led, larger-than-life reveal. Start with that visual energy for the ticket invitation; test it against TABLO’s more intimate treatment.
track2Body: TABLO describes the song as quiet comfort for his wife. Test a companionship-led invitation with the performance section and BANG YEDAM’s feature credit.
track3Body: MITHRA JIN’s NELL-produced song brings a singing-led contrast. Test that unexpected side for listening and for reflective, cleared morning-after recaps.
videoNote: The official EPIKASE episode contains performance chapters at 10:51, 28:02 and 41:33. These are references for the client’s creative team. The client supplies finished ad files with music/likeness rights and captions cleared before launch. Tour setlist inclusion is not assumed.
channelTitle: One paid platform. Two clear destinations.
channelBody: Run Meta ads across Instagram and Facebook Reels, Stories and Feed. Reach local music fans and reconnect with eligible audiences who have engaged with the artist or watched their videos. Give each city a clear invitation and a direct path to its ticket page.
channelBody2: Start with TUKUTZISM and anime, then test the member-led songs and client-supplied creative against ticket-page and listening-link response. Put more media behind the ads that best connect fans with the show or the release.
destination1Body: City-specific ad → official city ticket page. One primary action: get tickets. Use purchase optimization only when validated ticketing events and enough signal are available; otherwise measure ticket-page visits.
destination2Body: Song or recap ad → approved release smartlink. One primary action: listen. Use the existing official link initially; use the team’s measurable smartlink if analytics access is supplied. An outbound service click is not a completed stream.
waveIntro: Anticipation. The live moment. The return to the music. CCD’s “dopamine wave” connects the invitation to the show with a paid listening push after every tour market.
waveCaption: Conceptual campaign rhythm. Time is not to scale; particles do not represent people, sales or performance data.
waveBeforeBody: Client-supplied new-song ads earn attention; city, venue and date make the invitation concrete. The six priority flights run 14 days before each show. The expanded package adds five-day Los Angeles and Oakland bursts. Stop at the ticket cutoff, or earlier if sold out.
waveLiveBody: Artist Stories and available, cleared live footage can connect the evening to the release. Any promoter capture, venue placement or artist posting is discussed after campaign acceptance. No paid show-day ticket line or on-site crew is included.
waveAfterBody: Every market keeps a paid listening push: $100 over two days in the $10K package, or $200 over four days in the $15K package. Use an approved client-supplied release ad as the planned asset. A finished, cleared market recap can replace it when available. Seattle’s two nights share one flight after October 25. Consolidate local delivery when eligible engagement audiences are too small.
waveRule: One ad, one ask. The client can supply a new city/date/CTA version of a cleared recap for another included ticket market. Promoter participation, capture and recap delivery will be worked out after acceptance; the paid listening plan can run with approved client-supplied release ads.
marketsTitle:
Concentrate the spend.
Keep the whole tour in view.
marketsIntro: The September 2 ticket report now drives the plan. Prioritize remaining inventory and time to show, then adjust for approved assets and actual campaign response. Listening geography provides audience context alongside these dated sales counts.
geoSubtitle: Estimated Spotify monthly listeners by city • Sep 4, 2026
geoNote: Chartmetric modeled estimates, not ticket demand, unique targetable fans or observed city growth. The six other tour markets were absent from the returned 46-city sample; absence does not mean no audience. City boundaries can overlap, so totals are not added. The September 2 ticket report takes priority over this listening order.
scheduleNote: All 14 shows are upcoming as of September 7, 2026. Ticket counts are from the September 2 WME report supplied by the artist team; they are a dated planning snapshot. Ticket pages remain linked to the official sales destinations. Refresh counts before each flight.
soldoutNote: The September 2 WME report lists Seattle October 22 at 942 sold of 1,000 sellable, with 58 open, superseding the earlier sold-out report. It receives no ticket budget at 94.2% sold; prioritize October 25, with 545 open at 45.5% sold. Both nights share one paid listening flight after October 25.
priorityRule: Prioritize Atlanta, New York, Boston, Seattle October 25, Las Vegas and Dallas; add short Los Angeles and Oakland bursts in the $15K package. Adjust against fresh ticket counts and campaign response. If promoters fund agreed pre-show coverage, redirect the corresponding ticket-media allocation into post-show music marketing in those markets. Otherwise, agree any city scope swap and keep the base total fixed.
creativeTitle:
The ads should sound
like Epik High.
creativeIntro: Member chemistry, contrasting tracks and the EPIKASE battle give the client’s creative team a starting point. The following are strategic directions for client-produced ads. The artist’s team produces and supplies all final edits, city versions, format exports and approved English captions. CCD selects, tests and manages the supplied assets.
concept1Title: Your favorite group chat. In person.
concept1Hook: Use TUKUTZ’s dance-led performance reveal and the members’ comic chemistry, then cut into TUKUTZISM. Finish with the show’s city and date. The feeling is a reunion with the group, not a generic tour poster.
concept1Meta: 10–15 seconds • 9:16 + 4:5 • local fans and new music audiences • pre-show
concept1Copy: “Your favorite group chat. In person. Epik High · Atlanta · October 11.”
concept1Asset: Client asset brief: use the official TUKUTZISM performance chapter starting at 41:33 as a reference. Supply a finished city-specific ad with cleared music/likeness rights.
concept2Hook: TABLO frames anime around companionship and silent comfort. A subtitled introduction into the performance gives a friend-to-friend invitation a reason to exist.
concept2Meta: 15 seconds • 9:16 + 4:5 • artist engagers and local prospects • pre-show
concept2Copy: “Bring someone who gets it. Epik High · New York · September 30.”
concept2Asset: Client asset brief: the official anime chapter starts at 10:51. Supply the finished excerpt, city details and approved English captions. No promise that the track or its guest will appear in the tour set.
concept3Title: You know the voice. Hear another side.
concept3Hook: Let MITHRA JIN’s singing-led performance interrupt expectations. Use one song and one member per listening version, then make the destination explicit.
concept3Meta: 10–15 seconds • 9:16 + 4:5 • included package markets only • ongoing release
concept3Copy: “MITHRA JIN · Will I Be Okay. Hear another side.”
concept3Cta: Listen to Will I Be Okay
concept3Asset: Client asset brief: the official MITHRA JIN chapter starts at 28:02. Supply a finished listening ad using cleared performance footage or artwork/audio. The official song battle ends September 14; do not extend voting into the tour.
concept4Hook: When cleared footage is available, open with a moment from that city and use anime or Will I Be Okay as the soundtrack. Otherwise, use a client-supplied release ad to reconnect the night with an intentional listen.
concept4Meta: 10–20 seconds • 9:16 + 4:5 • eligible engagers in the played city • post-show
concept4Copy: “Last night stays with you. Take the night home.”
concept4Cta: Listen to Will I Be Okay
concept4Asset: The client supplies an approved, finished release ad for post-show use. A finished market recap using cleared artist, venue or fan footage can replace it when available. Any capture and recap delivery arrangements are agreed after acceptance; CCD does not produce or edit the assets.
creativeFoot: These are creative directions and sample copy for the client’s team to produce. All final creative, editing, localization, resizing, captions and recap production are the client’s responsibility. CCD provides campaign strategy, asset selection and media testing.
swshTitle:
Let the night
live in one place.
swshTag: Optional partner activation • outside both packages
swshIntro: A shared swsh album can turn scattered fan angles into a collective show memory, with a clear route back to EPIKASE. Start with a separately scoped two-show pilot only if the team can distribute and moderate it.
swshVerified: Verified: shared photo/video albums, link/QR entry, browser participation and custom outbound links. Commercial plans list analytics and custom upload agreements. Branded artist services require the appropriate commercial scope.
swshScope: Potential distribution includes artist Stories, a merch-table QR, venue-approved screens or an eligible promoter message. Discuss promoter participation and venue placement after Epik High accepts the campaign; neither is committed. If the pilot proceeds, the tour team supplies finished creative, secures placement and names a moderator. CCD coordinates campaign links within a separately agreed activation scope. The vendor configures albums and reporting exports. Any recap or listening-link follow-up requires agreed content, channel permissions and a sending platform.
swshRights: Three separate permissions: participating in the album; allowing specific content and recognizable likenesses to be reused, especially in ads; and choosing email/SMS marketing. Uploaders retain ownership under swsh terms. Download access is not an advertising license, and album membership is not marketing consent.
swshCost: Public plans list Starter at $100/month and Growth at $250/month; Enterprise is quoted. These are software entry prices, not an Epik High activation quote. Custom branding, moderation, rights work, participant capacity and CCD execution must be scoped separately. No vendor cost is hidden in either package.
swshNoPromise: An outbound music link is feasible. Native streaming attribution, automatic retargeting access and guaranteed engagement are not assumed. Confirm analytics/export definitions and applicable age, privacy and consent requirements before activating.
investmentIntro: All-in campaign investment in USD. Both the $10,000 and $15,000 totals include $1,000 for creator outreach and negotiation management. Campaign management is calculated at 15% of CCD-managed media spend. The remaining budget funds working media, and the artist’s team supplies all finished creative. Optional swsh and other vendors are scoped separately.
focusedDesc: Six priority ticket markets. Every city after the show.
expandedDesc: Deeper priority flights. Two finishing bursts.
focusedGeo: 14-day ticket flights: Atlanta, New York, Boston, Seattle (Oct 25), Las Vegas and Dallas. Paid post-show listening: all 13 markets.
expandedGeo: Larger 14-day flights in the same six priority markets. Five-day finishing bursts: Los Angeles and Oakland. Paid post-show listening: all 13 markets.
focusedDeliverables: CCD manages six priority ticket flights, pooled release support and two-day paid listening after all 13 markets. Includes campaign setup, link/tracking QA, optimization, reporting and creator outreach and negotiation management. The $1,000 creator service is included in the $10,000 total. The client supplies all finished assets.
expandedDeliverables: CCD manages six larger priority ticket flights, two finishing bursts, pooled release support and four-day paid listening after all 13 markets. Includes campaign setup, link/tracking QA, optimization, reporting and creator outreach and negotiation management. The $1,000 creator service is included in the $15,000 total. The client supplies all finished assets.
masterNote: Both packages include twice-weekly optimization, weekly reporting and a final readout. Before each flight, the client supplies launch-ready 9:16 and 4:5 files, city/date versions, approved captions and music/likeness clearances. Approved release ads support every post-show flight. Cleared, finished recaps can be used when available; promoter participation, capture and delivery arrangements are finalized after acceptance. Creative production and adaptation remain outside CCD’s scope.
deltaMediaBody: $2,800 more ticket media: $2,300 to deepen the six priority flights and $500 for Los Angeles and Oakland bursts. Add $247.82 to pooled release support and $1,300 to post-show listening, doubling each market’s listening flight from two days to four.
deltaCreativeBody: More testing of client-supplied assets across the six priority markets and two added finishing bursts. The client produces and delivers every creative version.
deltaMgmtBody: Management remains 15% of CCD-managed media spend in both campaigns, supporting deeper priority flights, two added ticket markets, longer listening flights and the additional optimization and reporting. The included creator management line stays at $1,000 in both totals.
mediaNote: 14-day ticket allocations ($10K / $15K): Atlanta $1,400 / $2,000; New York $1,100 / $1,500; Boston $700 / $1,000; Seattle October 25 $700 / $1,100; Las Vegas $800 / $1,300; Dallas $400 / $500. The $15K package also adds Los Angeles $300 over five days ($60/day) and Oakland $200 over five days ($40/day). Post-show listening averages $50/day: $100 per market over two days, or $200 over four.
poolNote: The $10K release pool is $1,426.09 across Sep 10–Oct 19 (about $35.65/day), rotating among its six priority ticket markets. The $15K pool is $1,673.91 across Sep 10–Oct 29 (about $33.48/day), rotating among its eight ticket markets. Each is one consolidated pool. Separate post-show flights cover all 13 markets, ending Oct 31 or Nov 2 respectively. Seattle’s two shows share one post-Oct 25 flight. This is the starting allocation; any promoter-funded shift into post-show marketing is agreed before activation.
exclusions: Excluded: creative production, editing, localization, resizing, captions, recap production, new shoots/on-site crews, media beyond the ceiling, cash creator fees, PR, guaranteed playlists, ticketing/platform fees, new landing pages, CRM builds, swsh, vendor moderation and fan-content rights procurement. Creator outreach and negotiation management is included as a $1,000 line in both campaign totals. The client supplies finished creative, usage clearances, ad access and destination links, including approved release ads for post-show use. Creator exchanges use team-provided complimentary tickets; cash talent fees and paid-ad reuse rights are separate. Promoter participation and any recap arrangements are discussed after acceptance. No ad launch or spend commitment is created by this proposal.
calendarAssumption: Planning start: September 10, assuming approvals and access by September 8. If onboarding timing or promoter coverage changes, confirm a revised schedule and allocation within the selected all-in budget before launch.
measureTitle:
Measure the action.
Respect the limits.
measureIntro: We commit to the scoped work and transparent decisions. Ticket sales, streams, followers and reach are observed outcomes. No modeled sales or streaming forecast is presented because no campaign-specific benchmark has been verified.
measureTicket: Report spend, impressions, reach, frequency, ticket-link visits and cost per visit by city. Call clicks “clicks” if destination landing-page measurement is unavailable. Report attributable purchases/return only after ticketing events are validated; otherwise use promoter-supplied city sales trends as context, not causal proof.
measureMusic: Report smartlink visits and outbound streaming-service clicks when access permits. Track all three release IDs, Epik High’s group profile and relevant member profiles. Compare first complete seven-day track windows, then like-for-like weekly windows; do not compare a partial release day with a full week. Artist trends use fixed-date, rolling 28-day listener snapshots and cumulative followers.
measureSwsh: Subject to the contracted dashboard/export: joins, unique uploaders, approved assets, assets cleared for organic/paid reuse, separate marketing opt-ins, and tagged listening-link activity. Define each denominator before reporting participation rates. An upload or opt-in does not prove a stream or sale.
optTitle: A weekly decision, not just a report.
opt1: Daily: check delivery, broken links, spend pacing and ticket status. Pause a sold-out show immediately. Before launch, test destinations and any purchase events with the ticketing partner.
opt2: Twice weekly: review each city’s ticket-page visits and listening-link activity. Compare client-supplied songs and creative over comparable periods, then refine the campaign around the strongest response.
opt3: Adjust the allocation as ticket availability and campaign response develop. Strengthen the markets and ads showing the clearest opportunity, and agree any change in city scope. Where a promoter funds pre-show coverage, use the agreed shift into post-show music marketing.
opt4: Weekly: reconcile media with city ticket reports, refresh song/artist snapshots and document changes. Final readout within five business days after the package ends. No ticket- or stream-sale guarantees.
nextTitle:
Choose the reach.
We’ll build the rhythm.
nextIntro: Choose the $10,000 or $15,000 all-in campaign. Both include creator outreach and negotiation management. We will finalize the agreement, refresh ticket priorities and confirm access. Promoter participation and any post-show capture arrangements can follow acceptance.
next1: Select the $10,000 or $15,000 all-in campaign, including the $1,000 creator outreach and negotiation management line.
next2: Refresh the September 2 ticket counts, confirm promoter-funded coverage where proposed, and agree city tracking links, account access and approved tracking.
next3: Supply launch-ready ads, city versions, captions, usage clearances and a release ad for post-show use. Confirm the team’s creator ticket allotment, smartlink reporting access and any available recap assets.
next4: Sign the scoped agreement, then authorize media launch separately.
emailNote: Opens an email draft to Crowd Control Digital. Nothing is sent, approved or charged automatically.
sourcesIntro: Proposal updated September 7, 2026 using the September 2 WME ticket report supplied by the artist team. Ticket counts and sellable capacity are dated figures, not live inventory. Music and audience research remains the September 4 snapshot. Proposed allocations, creator activity and post-show participation are planning decisions.

photoCaption: Official Epik High 3.0 tour press image • Seattle Theatre Group
sharedRecap: Shares Seattle’s listening flight after Oct 25
creatorTitle: Local voices. A night on us.
creatorIntro: Both campaign totals include $1,000 for outreach and negotiation management across the 13-market plan. Invite one local creator per market to make a short post using the new audio in exchange for a pair of tickets. Start with these music, dance and culture prospects, then qualify their recent content and local audience before inviting.
creatorOfferBody: Propose one original Reel or TikTok using cleared EPIKASE audio, posted 7–10 days before the show, plus a Story with the city ticket link where tickets remain. A post-show listening-link Story is an additional request to agree with each creator. Aim for one accepted creator per market, with up to 13 pairs of team-provided tickets. A collective invitation covers one designated creator and guest. The offer is tickets only; meet-and-greet access is not included. The artist team may independently choose and approve any such access separately. Adjust the CTA toward listening if the show sells out.
creatorAudio: Give each song a natural role
creatorAudioBody: TUKUTZISM: movement, concert prep or a night-out transition. anime: who you are bringing and why. Will I Be Okay: a personal reflection or the feeling after the show. Keep the creator’s own voice and one clear destination per post.
creatorScope: The $1,000 creator management line is included in both campaign totals. CCD qualifies the shortlist, handles outreach and ticket-exchange negotiations, agrees deliverables and posting dates, coordinates the brief and ticket handoff, and tracks delivery across the 13-market plan. These are researched prospects; availability and ticket-only acceptance are unconfirmed. Replace prospects who decline the agreed ticket offer. Cash talent fees, paid-ad reuse rights, professional shoots and full-crew production require separate approval and budget.
creatorRights: Agree post timing, ticket allocation and organic repost permission before confirming. Posts clearly disclose the complimentary tickets. Paid-ad reuse requires separate creator permission and music/likeness clearance. Confirm the creator’s publishing channel and local audience; do not assume a ticket exchange grants advertising rights.
creatorMeasure: Track accepted invitations, published posts, delivered links and available views, saves, shares and link activity. Report audience geography only when the creator supplies it. No guaranteed reach or acceptance.
waveReducedMotion: Motion is reduced. Select a phase or move the slider to explore.
waveBeforeDetail: New audio becomes a reason to choose the night.
waveLiveDetail: The shared live moment becomes the story.
waveAfterDetail: Paid listening brings every market back to the release.
creatorFeeBody: Included as a $1,000 line within either all-in campaign. Covers shortlist qualification, outreach, negotiation of the ticket-only exchange and deliverables, briefing, ticket coordination and post tracking across 13 markets. The team supplies complimentary tickets. Cash talent fees, content production and paid-ad reuse rights are separate. Campaign management is 15% of CCD-managed media spend, with both fees already included in the stated total.
creatorFeeTotal: Total investment remains $10,000 for Focused or $15,000 for Expanded, including the $1,000 creator management service.
ticketSnapshotTitle: Ticket counts now set the priorities.
ticketSnapshotNote: WME ticket report dated September 2, 2026, supplied by the artist team. Sellable capacity excludes comps and holds. Open equals sellable less sold; these are dated report counts, not live inventory. Refresh before each flight.
promoterPivotBody: When promoters fund pre-show advertising in agreed markets, CCD will redirect the corresponding ticket-media allocation into post-show music marketing in those same markets. Before funds move, promoters must confirm their funded coverage and use CCD-provided city ticket links with the agreed tracking.
promoterPivotTracking: CCD’s links measure each market’s campaign traffic. Approved site tracking and access to eligible ad-engagement audiences support local remarketing for the post-show listening campaign.
promoterPivotBudget: The all-in total stays at $10,000 or $15,000, including $1,000 for creator management and campaign management at 15% of CCD-managed media spend. The displayed allocations remain the starting plan until promoter coverage and tracking are confirmed. Agree increased post-show amounts and the delivery periods they require before activation. Use approved client-supplied release ads, with cleared recaps when available.
